key_insight: A HIPAA-compliant LLM workflow can automatically phenotype rare myeloproliferative neoplasms by combining EHR retrieval, text extraction, and guideline-based diagnosis/risk stratification.
clinical_relevance: This could reduce the manual burden of reviewing messy longitudinal records and help standardize diagnosis and prognostic scoring for rare hematologic malignancies.
method: Retrieved bone marrow biopsy reports, clinical notes, and lab results from the EHR
Used GPT-4 Turbo for zero-shot extraction of diagnostic and prognostic variables
Applied clinician-informed source prioritization plus WHO/ICC and NCCN-based classification/risk models
evidence_signal: In a held-out test set of 450 patients, performance was compared against dual-clinician chart review using metrics such as sensitivity, specificity, F1, and Cohen’s kappa, with bootstrap and Wilson confidence intervals.
watch_item: Results come from a retrospective single-framework evaluation, so real-world performance may vary with site-specific documentation quality, workflow integration, and changing guidelines.
paper_title: Automated Phenotypic Characterization in Rare Hematologic Malignancies Using a Large Language Model-Based Framework
